key_insight: Including solute mass transfer in droplet impact and solidification changes the predicted flow, mushy-zone evolution, and macrosegregation patterns in ways that better match experiments.
engineering_relevance: The model improves prediction of solidifying alloy splat shape and defect-prone segregation zones, which is important for additive manufacturing, thermal spray, and casting processes.
method: Fully coupled multiphysics solver for multiphase hydrodynamics, wetting, heat transfer, phase change, and solute transport
Concentration-flux-correction algorithm to enforce solute mass conservation at the discretization level
Validation against several benchmarks before simulating alloy droplet impact and solidification
evidence_signal: The abstract reports careful validation across several benchmarks and improved agreement with experimental observations when mass transfer is included.
watch_item: The approach adds model and numerical complexity, so accurate prediction depends on robust treatment of mushy-zone properties and solute-conservation enforcement.
paper_title: Numerical Modeling of a Metallic Alloy Droplet Impact, Solidification, and Macrosegregation
